text: . In the forex market today, the rupee strengthened by 62 paise to close at a seven-month high of 92 rupees and 67 paise against the US dollar. The rupee extended its rising streak for the fifth consecutive session following uninterrupted inflow of foreign funds and a rally in domestic stock markets.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 103.85 in intra-day trade.

. India and Nepal today inked eight agreements for collaboration in different fields. These are Health, traditional medicine, establishment of a satellite communication network, capacity-building training programme, sustainable urban development, Academic and research, and Livestock and Fisheries Development.  The agreements were signed after talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi.In his press statement, Mr Modi said, India-Nepal relations are woven together by shared history, faith, culture and deep people-to-people ties. He underlined that the relationship is not merely one of neighbours, but one of kinship and unbreakable trust. Mr Modi said, both nations are partners in each other’s progress and a source of support for each other in difficult times. He expressed condolences over the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August this year. The Prime Minister announced a Development Cooperation Package of 24, 000 crore Nepalese rupees to give renewed strength to Nepal’s reconstruction and long-term development.In his statement, Mr Shah said, India is a trusted partner of Nepal and the trust stands as high as the Himalayas. He said, India has always stood as the first responder during crisis. Mr Shah called for expanding air connectivity between both countries.After the talks both Prime Ministers witnessed demonstration of Railway Technologies and also a presentation on the Gatishakti Portal. Both leaders inaugurated motorable road bridge connecting Dharchula in India and Darchula in Nepal, and dedicated to the nation Motihari-Amlekhgunj pipeline (Phase-II). Mr Modi and Mr Shah also laid foundation stone for integrated check post at Banbasa, greenfield Oil storage terminal at Jhapa in Nepal and 669 megawatt lower Arun Hydroelectric Project in Kosho province in Nepal. Mr Modi and his Nepalese counterpart jointly flagged off the Saryu-Kamla express train between Ayodhya and Janakpur.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is holding bilateral talks with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah at Hyderabad House in New Delhi. Both leaders will review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest.The two Prime Ministers will virtually inaugurate several completed initiatives, apart from carrying out foundation stone laying ceremonies for some new projects. A number of forward-looking bilateral agreements in diverse areas are expected to be concluded and exchanged following the talks. The major outcomes are likely to be in the domains of development partnership, energy, hydropower, railways, connectivity, addressing climate change and disaster resilience, infrastructure, and technology.He was accorded a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan this morning. Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed him. The Nepal Prime Minister paid his respects to Mahatma Gandhi by laying wreath at Rajghat. He will call on President Droupadi Murmu later this afternoon. The visiting dignitary arrived in the national capital yesterday on a two-day visit.

. In Hockey, India defeated South Korea 2-1 in their second league stage match of Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal yesterday evening. For India, Mumtaz Khan scored the first goal, while Sunelita Toppo scored India’s second goal. Hong Youngeun scored only goal for South Korea. Indian player Navneet Kaur was named Player of the Match. This was India’s second consecutive win in the tournament.Earlier in the day, Japan registered a convincing 3-nil victory over Thailand in their league stage encounter, while China and Malaysia played out a 2-2 draw. India will play its next match against Thailand today. The team will then face China on November 24 and Japan on November 25. The league stage will continue until November 25. Position matches will be played on November 27, followed by the bronze medal and gold medal matches on November 28.

. Market participants will focus on geopolitical developments, the final leg of the corporate earnings season, foreign portfolio investor (FPI) flows, commodity price movements and currency fluctuations for cues next week.Indian equity markets will remain closed on Tuesday on account of Gurpurab, the birth anniversary of Sri Guru Nanak Dev. Meanwhile, on the primary market front, two mainboard IPOs are scheduled to open for subscription, while two companies are set to make their stock market debut.In the United States, investors will closely monitor the upcoming Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data, along with the second estimate of third-quarter GDP growth. Meanwhile, market participants will also keep a close watch on the Bank of Korea’s upcoming monetary policy decision for cues on the global interest rate outlook.

. India’s capital markets have mobilised nearly 9 lakh crore rupees in the first seven months of the current financial year, while market capitalisation has crossed the 5 trillion-dollar mark. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey has announced further regulatory reforms to attract foreign investment and simplify access to the country’s capital markets.Addressing the CII-DFS Financing Summit 2026 in Mumbai today, Mr Pandey said companies have raised an average of around 10 lakh crore rupees annually through equity and debt instruments over the past decade. He attributed the expansion to strong economic growth, rising investor participation and sustained regulatory reforms. More than 15 crore unique investors are now participating in the securities market.Highlighting the buoyancy in the primary market, the SEBI Chairman said 235 companies have raised around 1.5 lakh crore rupees through Initial Public Offerings so far in the current financial year.He said the corporate bond market is also emerging as an important source of business financing. Outstanding corporate bonds stood at around 62 lakh crore rupees in August this year, equivalent to nearly 55 per cent of bank credit extended to the industry and services sectors. Companies have raised more than 5 lakh crore rupees through bond issuances in FY 2026-27 so far.Mr Pandey also highlighted the growing contribution of Alternative Investment Funds in financing emerging businesses. Their cumulative investments reached around 7.5 lakh crore rupees by September, while committed capital exceeded 18 lakh crore rupees. Assets managed by Real Estate Investment Trusts and Infrastructure Investment Trusts have also crossed 10 lakh crore rupees, supporting infrastructure financing and capital recycling.On regulatory reforms, Mr Pandey said SEBI will soon release a consultation paper proposing further simplification of operations for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs), including the removal of certain compliance requirements that are not prevalent in other major markets.He said the regulator is working to reduce the FPI onboarding period to as little as five business days. Around 740 FPIs have registered under the Swagat framework, accounting for 17 per cent of total FPI assets under custody.As part of the simplification measures, SEBI has digitised onboarding, permitted digitally signed powers of attorney and enabled net settlement to reduce funding costs. From 1st December, KYC review cycles for applicable FPIs will be extended from one and three years to two and eight years, respectively. Eligible NRIs, overseas citizens of India and foreign nationals can also complete their KYC and re-KYC digitally without travelling to India.Outlining future priorities, Mr Pandey said SEBI is reviewing ICDR and LODR frameworks to eliminate duplicate corporate filings and introduce a single-fine mechanism. It is also working with the RBI and Finance Ministry on a corporate bond market-making framework, reducing REIT and InvIT listing timelines to three working days, and expanding AI-based regulatory tools.On investor safety, he highlighted 45-minute disaster-recovery mandates, SEBI Check, validated UPI handles, and the nationwide ‘Samajh Se Investing Simple’ awareness campaign.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and  Prime Minister of Nepal Balendra Shah today jointly flagged off the new weekly train service between Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh and Janakpur Dham in Nepal through video conferencing from New Delhi. The train service, named Saryu- Kamala Express, introduced by Indian Railways, began its inaugural run from Ayodhya Dham Railway Station.Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath attended the event at Ayodhya Dham Station. The train service will establish an important rail link between two destinations deeply associated with the Ramayana tradition – Janakpur Dham, revered as the birthplace of Mata Sita, and Ayodhya, the birthplace of Lord Shri Ram.The regular weekly service will cover a distance of 604 kilometres while passing through important towns and cities of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. The train will have key stoppages at Gorakhpur, Basti, Raxaul, Sitamarhi, Madhubani and Jaynagar. It will facilitate religious journeys between Janakpur and Ayodhya, encourage tourism circuits associated with the Ramayana and provide greater mobility to people travelling for education, business and family-related purposes.Akashvani correspondent reports that it is a major step of Indian Railways towards strengthening cross-border connectivity, religious tourism and India-Nepal Friendship. Akashvani correspondent reports that the Saryu- Kamala Express is more than a modern rail connection between two important destinations, as it provides an opportunity for pilgrims, tourists and visitors to experience the sacred heritage of Ayodhya and Janakpur through a convenient and comfortable train journey. The train will have eight AC  and seven sleeper coaches.The  Saryu- Kamala Express will operate once a week, with its originating days being  Monday from Ayodhya Cantt. and Saturday from Janakpur Dham. From Ayodhya Cantt., the weekly train will depart at 05.50 PM and reach Janakpur Dham at 12.40 PM the next day. In the return direction, the train will leave at 01.10 PM from Janakpur Dham and reach Ayodhya Cantt. at 08.10 AM. India and Nepal share centuries-old cultural, historical and social bonds, with religious traditions and cross-border community relationships forming an integral part of this partnership. The new train service will add another dimension to bilateral cooperation by using railway connectivity to bring communities closer.

. Fresh incidents of arson, crude bomb explosions and industrial unrest were reported in different parts of Bangladesh on Monday, according to local media reports. In Narayanganj, miscreants set fire to a passenger bus and a truck carrying garment waste in two separate incidents early Monday.The bus was torched in the Signboard area on the Dhaka-Chattogram Highway, while the truck was set ablaze in Fatullah. Fire service personnel brought both fires under control. In Old Dhaka, a 45-year-old Dhaka University gardener was seriously injured when a crude bomb exploded after falling on his head outside Kabi Nazrul Government College. He was admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital. Earlier, two crude bombs exploded outside Abudharr Ghifari College in Malibagh, although no injuries were reported.Meanwhile, an alleged attempt to set fire to a Chittagong University shuttle train at Bot Toli Railway Station was foiled. Railway authorities intervened before any damage occurred.In Gazipur, garment workers attempted to block the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway at several locations in Sreepur on Monday. Police fired tear gas to disperse the protesters, while 12 garment factories declared holidays amid tensions.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s dedicated Health Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 in New Delhi is showcasing its flagship health programmes and public healthcare initiatives. The theme of this year’s Health Pavilion is Yuva Bharat, Swasth Bharat, highlights preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and youth participation in building a healthier nation. The Pavilion was inaugurated by NITI Aayog Member, Dr M Srinivas, in the presence of Health Secretary, Punya Salila Srivastava.Addressing the gathering, Dr. Srinivas emphasised on preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyle choices to address rising burden of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and lifestyle-related health conditions. He also highlighted the importance of public awareness, early detection and timely medical intervention in preventing and managing NCDs. Outlining the benefits of Health Pavilion, Dr. Srinivas said that it offers a valuable opportunity for citizens to learn about common health risks, understand preventive measures and familiarise themselves with various Government healthcare programmes and services. He also encouraged visitors to actively participate in the Pavilion’s activities and use the opportunity to enhance their understanding of health and well-being.The Ministry noted that in the Pavilion 39 stalls representing 24 national health programmes and organisations showcase Government’s healthcare initiatives, achievements and services. The Ministry also highlighted that a dedicated TB stall has been established to raise awareness about tuberculosis and TB screening is being conducted using AI-enabled handheld X-ray technology. The Pavilion also included interactive activities, live cpr demonstrations, health awareness sessions and dedicated kids’ zone to engage visitors and promote healthy living. The Ministry said that the Pavilion provides an important platform to connect directly with citizens, showcase the Government’s wide-ranging healthcare initiatives and promote greater public awareness about preventive healthcare, early diagnosis and healthier lifestyles.

. Under the theme ‘Vikas Aur Virasat’ (Development and Heritage), women-led Self-Help Groups (SHGs) from Tripura, along with various wings under the Department of Industries and Commerce, are participating in the international trade fair being held in New Delhi.At the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, the Tripura Pavilion is showcasing a wide range of products manufactured by the state’s Self-Help Groups, along with an impressive collection of bamboo and cane handicrafts.Tripura Industries and Commerce Minister Santana Chakma visited the state’s stalls and encouraged the women entrepreneurs, appreciating their efforts. She said their contribution is significant in strengthening Tripura’s economy. She further stated that participation in such fairs would help promote products manufactured in Tripura and increase their recognition in the global market.It may be mentioned that Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal inaugurated the fair on November 13. The exhibition will continue until November 27, with participation from representatives of more than 30 states and Union Territories across the country.

. The combined Index of Core Industries (ICI) registered growth of 10.9 per cent in October on an annual basis driven by strong performance in iron ore, coal, electricity and cement sectors. This is higher than the upwardly revised growth rate of 8.2 per cent recorded in September. According to the provisional estimates released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry today, six out of nine core sectors recorded positive growth last month. Among these, iron ore production recorded the highest growth at 26.4 per cent. Coal production accelerated by 23.1 per cent, electricity generation increased by 21.6 per cent, cement production gained 15.4 per cent, steel production output grew by 7.3 per cent, and refinery products expanded by 3.4 per cent on an annual basis. However, natural gas production fell by 7.6 per cent, crude oil production dipped by 4.1 per cent, and fertilizer production declined by 12.2 per cent in October on an annual basis.

. A journey of friendship between India and Sri Lanka, inspired by their shared civilisational and Buddhist heritage, has completed its Sri Lankan leg in Jaffna. The Maitri Setu Yatra, the India-Sri Lanka NCC cycling expedition 2027, was flagged off from Galle Face in Colombo on November 15. Over the past week, the cyclists covered nearly 500 kilometres, travelling through Kurunegala, Dambulla, Anuradhapura, Vavuniya and Kilinochchi before reaching Jaffna in Sri Lanka.The Sri Lankan leg is part of an approximately 3,500-kilometre expedition. From Karaikal, the cyclists will continue across India, covering around 3,000 kilometres to New Delhi, where the journey is expected to culminate in Delhi in January 2027.The expedition seeks to strengthen India-Sri Lanka friendship through youth engagement, discipline and endurance, drawing inspiration from the countries’ deep historical, cultural and Buddhist connections.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal during the next five days. Met Department has predicted isolated to scattered rainfall in East Uttar Pradesh till tomorrow. Met Department has predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds in Andhra Pradesh and Andaman and Nicobar Islands today.IMD said Bihar, East Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura and Odisha are likely to witness dense fog. National Capital is experiencing light haze and a winter chill during the morning hours.

. Major Asian stock market indices edged lower today. Taiwan’s Taiex shed over 6.2 per cent, South Korea’s Kospi slumped 5.2 per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell almost 5.1 per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times dipped nearly 2.1 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dropped 1.9 per cent, and China’s Shanghai Composite dipped 1.2 per cent.On the economic front, Japan’s consumer price index (CPI) rose to 2.3 per cent year-on-year in October, up from 2.1 per cent in September. Consumer prices exceeded the Bank of Japan’s two per cent target for the second straight month. Meanwhile, the core CPI, which strips out prices of food, rose to 2.2 per cent last month on an annual basis, higher than 2.1 per cent in the previous month.In European markets, Germany’s DAX dipped 1.8 per cent, and London’s FTSE 100 dropped half a per cent, when reports last came in.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Similar conditions are expected over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura tomorrow.Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mist and shallow fog at most places of Delhi during the morning hours tomorrow.The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the ‘ Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 303 as of 7 PM today.

. In Tamil Nadu, eight people were killed and two others injured when the vehicle in which they were travelling lost control and crashed into a roadside tree near Musiri in Tiruchirappalli district yesterday. About ten people of a family were returning home after a family function in Namakkal District. Five people were killed on the spot, and three more succumbed to their injuries at the hospital. Two others are being treated for injuries at a nearby hospital. The police have registered a case. The case is under investigation.President Droupadi Murmu, Vice-President C P Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have expressed grief over the loss of lives in a road accident in Tiruchirappalli district of Tamil Nadu. In a social media post, the President prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured.Prime Minister announced an ex gratia of 2 lakh rupees from the Prime Minister’s National Relief Fund to the next of kin of each deceased. The injured will recieve 50 thousand rupees.

. The fourth day of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 in Goa is witnessing a diverse celebration of cinema, with films exploring themes of peace, compassion and intercultural understanding. A major highlight of today’s festival is the competition for the prestigious ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal, with ten Indian and international feature films vying for the honour.The selection includes three Indian entries – Kabir Sir ka Akhri Lesson, Scroll and Sev Micchar – alongside seven international films. Akashvani correspondent reports thatinstituted in collaboration with the International Council for Film, Television and Audiovisual Communication (ICFT), Paris, under the aegis of UNESCO, the award recognises films that reflect Mahatma Gandhi’s ideals of non-violence, tolerance, intercultural understanding and peaceful coexistence. Talking to media, Turkish filmmaker Elif Ada shared the humanitarian themes explored in her film The Farm, which is competing for the prestigious Gandhi Medal. Ada said the film explores compassion through the perspective of a twelve-year-old child who is distressed by the separation of newborn calves from their mothers.The fourth day of IFFI also featured a panel discussion on ‘Goa in Cinema’, with filmmaker Abhishek Pathak and actress Marianne, exploring the representation of Goa through cinema and its cultural significance. While, an In Conversation session titled ‘The Epic Genres – Mythologies, Superheroes and New Worlds’, featuring filmmaker Ayan Mukerji and actor-director Basil Joseph, is scheduled for later in the day.

. The 45th Indian International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will begin tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue. Visitors can also reach Bharat Mandapam through app-based taxis, private vehicles and public transport. He added that parking facilities for around three thousand vehicles have been arranged, along with designated waiting areas for app-based taxis. Special facilities, including wheelchair assistance will also be available for senior citizens to ensure a comfortable and convenient experience.

. At the National Squash Championships 2026, Abhay Singh and Akanksha Salunkhe clinched singles titles. They were crowned the men’s and women’s champions at the National Squash Championships 2026, which concluded at the Otters Club in Mumbai yesterday. This was the 82nd edition of the senior squash nationals.Top seed Abhay Singh, who won a silver medal at the Asian Games 2026, got the better of second seed Veer Chotrani 3-0  in the men’s final. It was a third senior national title for world No. 26 Abhay, who was contesting his fifth consecutive final. Akanksha Salunkhe, meanwhile, came through qualifying to lift her first senior national crown on her third attempt, having lost her two previous finals.

. The Delhi Traffic Police has issued a traffic advisory for today in view of the Nagar Keertan procession being organised by the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee. The procession will commence from Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib at 10 AM and culminate at Gurudwara Nanak Pio Sahib, GT Karnal Road. Delhi Traffic Police said that approximately 25 thousand to 30 thousand devotees and around 500 vehicles are expected to participate in the procession. It has been informed that Old GT Karnal Road and Bhama Shah Road will remain closed to traffic today from 5 PM till 12 midnight.Traffic may also be regulated or diverted, depending upon the prevailing traffic conditions, at locations including Stadium Road T-Point, Sant Kripal Singh T-Point, Ashok Vihar Flyover, Kripal Bagh Red Light, Derawal Nagar T-Point, Bhama Shah Chowk, Swami Narayan Underpass, Rana Pratap Bagh Colony Gate, Raj Kumar Kaushik Marg T-Point, Maharaja Agrasen Marg and GTK Road T-Point. The Traffic Police advised commuters to plan their journeys in advance and allow additional travel time. It also asked motorists to avoid non-essential travel through affected areas, follow diversion signs and directions of traffic personnel, and cooperate with Delhi Traffic Police to ensure smooth traffic movement.

. Union Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav today highlighted that the frontline staff and local communities are the backbone of India’s wildlife conservation efforts. The Minister chaired the 92nd Meeting of the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife in New Delhi. Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change said that the Standing Committee considered the report on Wildlife Week 2026, celebrated under the theme Connecting Habitats, Thriving Wildlife.During the meeting, the Minister highlighted the initiatives taken during Wildlife Week 2026, including the tiger reintroduction in Buxa, the release of Great Indian Bustards in Rajasthan and the expansion of Project Cheetah to a third site. The Ministry said that the meeting was themed on marine conservation. During the meeting, several publications highlighting the Ministry’s conservation initiatives relating to marine biodiversity conservation were released. The Minister also released a document pertaining to small cat conservation, covering nine species of small cats found in the country.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

On the first day of the 43rd Indian Oil Servo Surjit Hockey Tournament in Jalandhar yesterday, the Pool A match between former champions Indian Oil Mumbai and BSF Jalandhar ended in a 1- 1 draw.Bharat Petroleum registered a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Punjab National Bank (PNB), Delhi, in a Pool-B league match.In Pool-D, the Indian Air Force team delivered an impressive performance, securing victory over Punjab & Sind Bank, Delhi, 2-1.

. India’s Under-20 boys’ kabaddi team began their campaign at the Four-Nation Cup Kabaddi Championship 2026 in Kathmandu with a convincing 76-21 victory over Bangladesh, winning by a margin of 55 points.In another match, hosts Nepal defeated Thailand 56-50 to register a six-point victory. India currently tops the points table, while Nepal occupies the second position.The tournament features four teams- India, Nepal, Bangladesh and Thailand. Under the tournament format, each team will play the other teams once in a six-match league stage, with the top two teams qualifying for the final tomorrow.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) yesterday proposed eliminating additional disclosure requirements for offshore funds, arguing that existing beneficial ownership disclosure norms already provide adequate transparency and oversight. The proposal marks a significant shift from regulations introduced in 2023, when the market regulator tightened scrutiny of offshore investment structures. Under the current framework, offshore funds considered to be at higher risk are required to make enhanced disclosures, including details of their ultimate beneficial owners.The regulator said the proposed changes are aimed at balancing regulatory oversight with ease of doing business while ensuring that capital markets remain attractive to foreign investors. The proposal has been put forward for public consultation, and feedback from market participants is expected before SEBI takes a final decision on amending the framework.

. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold plunged nearly 4.4 per cent to 1,23,893 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, silver also tumbled over 4.9 per cent to 1,52,528 rupees per kilogram according to the closing rates of India Bullion and Jewellers Association.

. In Mizoram, three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival is underway in south Mizoram’s Lunglei town, bringing together established musicians, emerging bands and local entrepreneurs to showcase the state’s musical heritage and promote tourism. Organised by the Ministry of Tourism and Mizoram Tourism department, the festival began yesterday at Lena Stadium at Serkawn under the theme “Music Comes Home to Serkawn”. The festival seeks to connect that legacy with contemporary musicians and emerging talent.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said music was an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity and Serkawn held a special place in the state’s musical history. The minister said that the government aimed to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to national and international audiences while creating opportunities for young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities. The festival features performances by established and emerging Mizo musicians.The second day includes a band competition with 10 finalists from Aizawl, Lunglei, Nagaland and Assam, while winners of the previous two editions, Swordtune and Knot, are also scheduled to perform. The final day will feature performances by several Mizo artists and bands, followed by the minister’s address and a fireworks display.

. In the bullion market, gold and silver prices witnessed a steep decline over the past week as a stronger US dollar and elevated Treasury yields weighed heavily on investor sentiment. For the second week in a row, precious metals remained under pressure as expectations grew that the US Federal Reserve would maintain its hawkish stance to bring inflation back within its 2 per cent target range.At the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), Gold futures for December contract plunged 10.9 per cent to settle at 1 lakh 21 thousand 778 rupees per 10 grams during the week. Silver futures for December contract tumbled almost 16.2 per cent to close at 1 lakh 47 thousand 813 rupees per kilogram.Meanwhile, at the Commodity Exchange (COMEX), Gold futures for the December contract plummeted 9.5 per cent during the week to settle at 3515.4 dollars per troy ounce. Silver futures for the December contract nosedived 16.4 per cent over the week to end at 41.07 dollars per troy ounce.

. In Indonesia, 24 people have reportedly been killed in a major fire at a confectionery factory in the Banten province. The fire broke out on Saturday afternoon. About 30 people are still missing as search operations continue. Police are using DNA samples, personal belongings, and forensic teams to identify remains, a process expected to take two to three weeks. Authorities were still investigating the cause of the fire.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today chaired the ninth Pre-Budget Consultation with  experts and stakeholders from the housing, urbanisation, and culture sectors in connection with the Union Budget 2027-28, in New Delhi. The meeting was also attended by Secretaries of Department of Economic Affairs and Department of Urban Development.Earlier in the day, the Finance Minister chaired the eighth Pre-Budget Consultation with the stakeholders from employment and labour sectors in connection with the upcoming Union Budget. The meeting was attended by Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs, Anuradha Thakur and senior officials from Ministry of Labour and Employment.The Finance Ministry conducts several pre-Budget consultation meetings annually with experts, industry leaders, economists, and state officials. The deliberations seek to ensure the Union budget reflects diverse perspectives and addresses key economic priorities.

. Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) sector has suffered losses worth 428 million US dollars following 18 days of labour unrest and industrial disruptions in November, with more than 250 million dollars worth of confirmed export orders reportedly shifted to other countries, according to local media reports. The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said a survey of 317 member factories found that production had remained suspended for periods ranging from one to 16 days between November 1 and 18, resulting in direct losses of 428 million dollars in Free on Board (FOB) value.The association said international buyers had shifted orders for around 59 million garments, valued at 254 million dollars, to competing countries amid concerns over stability and delivery commitments.According to BGMEA, the survey represents only part of the overall impact, as more than 600 factories have reportedly been affected by the unrest. The disruptions have also increased the risk of order cancellations, price discounts and additional air-freight costs as manufacturers struggle to meet delivery deadlines.The association warned that prolonged instability could further damage Bangladesh’s reputation as a reliable global apparel supplier and undermine the sector’s future competitiveness. Calling for urgent action, BGMEA urged all stakeholders to work together to restore industrial stability and ensure uninterrupted operations in the garment sector, which provides livelihoods to millions of workers and remains a major contributor to the country’s export earnings.

. In Men’s Cricket, New Zealand scored 119 for 2 at stumps on Day Four of the first Test against India in their second innings at Wellington.Earlier, the Visitors declared their first innings at a record 720 for 9, taking a huge lead of 352 runs over New Zealand’s first-innings score of 368. India’s total of 720 is their highest-ever Test score outside India and the 18th-highest total in Test cricket history.India also created two major records and became the first team to have their top five batters score 80 or more runs in the same innings. They also became the first team to build partnerships of 50 or more runs for each of the first seven wickets.For Visitors, KL Rahul played a key role at the top of the order. He became the first Indian opener to score a Test century in all four SENA countries South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.

. In Mumbai, more than 22,500 runners, including 59 participants from 20 foreign countries, took part in the ninth edition of the Indian Oil Western Naval Command (WNC) Navy Half Marathon 2026. The event was flagged off from Cross Maidan by Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Western Naval Command. Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan also participated in the 21-km race.The marathon featured three categories: 21 km, 10 km and 5 km. The event aims to promote fitness, patriotism and camaraderie between the Indian Navy and civilians.

. Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Jitan Ram Manjhi today inaugurated the MSME Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026 in New Delhi. On the occasion, Mr Manjhi interacted with artisans and exhibitors at various stalls. He highlighted the importance of khadi as a symbol of country’s rich cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship. The Minister said that khadi represents country’s traditional industry, entrepreneurship and art. Mr Manjhi also highlighted the PM Vishwakarma Yojana, which covers 18 traditional trades, including barbers, leather artisans, cobblers, garland makers and net weavers.

. In Hockey, India thrashed Thailand 7-0 in their league-stage encounter of the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal this evening. Deepika led the charge with a brilliant hat-trick, while Navneet Kaur scored a brace.Mumtaz Khan and skipper Sunelita Toppo also scored one goal each. This was India’s third consecutive victory in the tournament, following their earlier wins over Malaysia and South Korea. With this win, India moved to the top of the points table with nine points.Earlier in the day, Malaysia registered a 3-1 victory over South Korea in their league-stage match, while Japan also secured a convincing 3-1 win against China.

. In Table Tennis, India’s Boys Under-19 team has confirmed its first medal at the ITTF World Youth Championships in Istanbul, Türkiye, after storming into the semifinals. The Indian trio of Priyanuj Bhattacharya, Abhinandh Pradhivadhi and Balamurugan Rajasekaran produced a dominant performance, defeating hosts Türkiye 3-nil in the quarterfinals to seal a place in the last four and guarantee a medal for India. India will now face Chinese Taipei in the semifinals.Meanwhile, Indian Girls’ Under-19 team bowed out in the quarterfinals after suffering a nil-3 defeat to France. Divyanshi, Syndrela and Hansini lost their respective matches.

. In Men’s Cricket, the first Test between New Zealand and India ended in a draw. In reply to India’s 720 for 9 in first innings, New Zealand made 239 for 5 in their second innings. Akashvani correspondent reports that resuming the final day at 119 for two, Kiwis lost two well-set overnight batters in Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra. However, Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips stood firm for 43 overs as New Zealand batted out 120 overs in their second innings to salvage a draw in the first Test today.India had taken a 352-run first-innings lead after posting their highest-ever Test total in New Zealand, but could manage only three of the eight wickets they needed on the final day. The Visitors declared their first innings at a record 720 for 9, taking a huge lead of 352 runs over New Zealand’s first-innings score of 368. India also created two major records and became the first team to have their top five batters score 80 or more runs in the same innings.They also became the first team to build partnerships of 50 or more runs for each of the first seven wickets. For Visitors, KL Rahul played a key role at the top of the order. He became the first Indian opener to score a Test century in all four SENA countries South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.

. Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrived in New Delhi this afternoon on a two-day visit to India. This is his first visit to India after assuming office in March this year. He was received at the airport by Union Minister Jitin Prasada. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar called on the visiting dignitary this evening. In a social media post, Dr Jaishankar said India cherishes the special friendship with Nepal.Tomorrow, the Nepal Prime Minister will be given a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan. He will pay his respects to Mahatma Gandhi by laying a wreath at Rajghat. He will call on President Droupadi Murmu and hold a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. During the bilateral talks, both the leaders will review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest. The two Prime Ministers will virtually inaugurate several completed initiatives apart from carrying out foundation stone laying ceremonies for some new projects. A number of forward-looking bilateral documents in diverse areas are expected to be concluded and exchanged.Prime Minister Narendra Modi had extended an invitation to Prime Minister Balendra Shah to visit India after the new government assumed office in Nepal earlier this year, which was accepted by the Nepali side. This is Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s first bilateral visit abroad. Following interactions over the phone and exchange of social messages, this will be the first in-person meeting between the two leaders. This visit comes at an opportune moment when there is considerable synergy between the national priorities of both countries in terms of economic growth, social development, expansion of infrastructure, adoption of technology, and addressing issues like natural disasters and climate change.Discussions between the two leaders will provide a political direction which is expected to chart the course for the bilateral partnership for the coming years. The major outcomes are likely to be in the domains of development partnership, energy, hydropower, railways, connectivity, addressing climate change and disaster resilience, infrastructure, and technology.

. The Publications Division (DPD), under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, is drawing the attention of book lovers and cinema enthusiasts at the 57th International Film Festival of India with its diverse collection of publications. A major highlight of the Division’s participation this year has been the release of two significant books on Indian cinema.The first is ‘Cinema: Vividh Aayam’, compiled by Rajendra Bhatt and the other one is Awtar Kaul: The (In)Complete Story’, authored by Vinod Kaul, which chronicles the life and unfinished creative journey of filmmaker Awtar Kaul through personal letters, photographs, memories and conversations.Apart from books on Cinema, the stall showcases books on India’s rich cultural heritage, history, art, literature and cinema, offering festival delegates an opportunity to explore the country’s literary and cinematic legacy beyond the screen.

. Producer of the Spanish film Trinidad, Silvia Carvalho has appreciated the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) for providing a platform for diverse cinematic narratives from across the world.Talking to Akashvani News in Goa, she said the film explores a woman’s journey of taking control of her own destiny, blending adventure, humour and emotions. She added that she is delighted to be part of IFFI and looks forward to sharing the film with Indian audiences, noting that its themes have the potential to connect with viewers across cultures.

. Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar is holding talks with Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands, Tom Berendsen in New Delhi.In his opening remarks, Dr Jaishankar said that India and the Netherlands had elevated ties to a Strategic Partnership and the roadmap forged by both countries allows the pathway to proceed forward. He said their discussions today will cover several areas including water, health, and agriculture as well as newer areas like defence, technology, semiconductors, and renewable energy. He noted that 2027 will be the 80th anniversary of India-Netherlands diplomatic ties.Mr Berendsen reached New Delhi this afternoon on a two day visit to India. The Netherlands Foreign Affair Minister will also meet Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw tomorrow.

. Two films from the Northeast were showcased at the 57th edition of the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today.The films included Red Carpet, a documentary directed by Assam-based filmmaker Aimee Boruah, and Urum, a film by Duyu Tabyo from Arunachal Pradesh.Speaking to reporters, the filmmakers expressed happiness over the opportunity to showcase their works at one of the country’s premier film festivals, describing it as an encouragement for emerging filmmakers from the region.They said the recognition would inspire young talent and provide an impetus to the growth of the film industry in the Northeast.Highlighting the region’s rich cultural heritage and scenic landscapes, the filmmakers said the Northeast had immense potential as a destination for filmmaking but remained largely unexplored.The directors also emphasised the need to bring the region’s diverse traditions and cultural identity to a wider global audience.Despite being at a relatively nascent stage, the film industry in the Northeast has considerable potential, with several talented filmmakers emerging from the region, they said, adding that the industry was gradually gaining momentum.

. Assamese filmmaker Antara G.G. Choudhury today expressed happiness and gratitude over the selection of her directorial debut Surjyamukhi, in the Indian Panorama section of the 57th International Film Festival of India. Talking to Akashvani News, she said that the film explores contemporary Assamese society, focusing on the choices, aspirations and human relationships of young people. Explaining the title, she noted that the film’s central concept is about people supporting one another, just as sunflowers symbolise togetherness and mutual support in her interpretation.

. Anupama Ramachandran clinched her second consecutive world title at the IBSF World Women’s Snooker Championship in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, yesterday. She defeated Hong Kong’s So Man Yan 3-1 in the final to successfully retain her crown, which she won last year to become India’s first-ever female IBSF Snooker world champion. After conceding a 16-58 defeat in the first frame, Anupama bounced back to win the next three frames dominantly to conquer the title in front of a home crowd.

. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports will organise the ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad on the occasion of Constitution Day, through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) in more than 500 colleges across the country. The three-day Samvad will begin tomorrow. The Ministry said that the nationwide initiative aims to connect young people in the age group of 15-29 years with India’s developmental journey, its achievements and aspirations for the future. It said that the initiative will inspire them to become active participants in the nation’s transformation into a developed country by 2047. Participants across institutions will collectively undertake a reading of the Preamble to the Constitution. The programme will also provide a nationwide platform for engaging young people through interactive dialogues and awareness sessions.

. Secretary of the Union Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Dr. Saurabh Garg, today said that City Economic Product will soon be released in the country. He said that cities are drivers of economic growth and this index will reflect it more effectively. He was speaking at a Data User conference in Mumbai to provide information about revised methods of measuring GDP, Consumer Price Index and Index of Industrial Production, and their new base year. He said that many states have adopted the new base year to measure the state’s Gross Domestic Product and others will also adopt it soon. Mr. Garg informed that revised guidelines will soon be implemented to make the District Domestic Product more effective.

. World Fisheries Day is being observed today. The day aims to highlight the importance of sustainable fisheries and aquaculture in ensuring food and nutritional security, generating livelihoods and maintaining ecological balance. The observance traces its origins to 1997, when representatives from 18 countries gathered in New Delhi to establish the World Fisheries Forum. The initiative aimed to promote responsible fishing practices and safeguard the rights and interests of fishing communities.The theme for World Fisheries Day 2026 is “Empowering People for Change: Advancing Decent Work in Fisheries and Aquaculture, Particularly for Youth and Women.” The theme highlights the need to promote decent employment opportunities, empower women and young people, and ensure inclusive and sustainable growth across the fisheries and aquaculture sectors.India is the world’s second-largest fish-producing country, accounting for nearly eight per cent of global fish production. The country has made significant progress in the sector over the past decade. India’s total fish production has more than doubled, rising from 96 lakh tonnes to 195 lakh tonnes last year. The fisheries sector is an important pillar of the Indian economy, supporting the livelihoods of millions of people. A coordinated approach involving all stakeholders is aimed at further strengthening the sector, with a focus on increasing fish production, boosting exports and creating more livelihood opportunities.

. This year’s United Nations Climate Change Conference, COP31, at Antalya, Turkiye, ended yesterday with no agreement for the first time since 2009. The UN climate talks collapsed without an overarching agreement after deep disagreements over whether to explicitly mention fossil fuels in the final text. European Union and several other countries rejected the proposed deal, saying it is too weak to advance the fight against climate change.The two-week negotiations, known as COP31, continued nearly 48 hours beyond their scheduled conclusion, making them the longest COP on record. However, countries failed to reach a consensus on a main agreement, known as a cover decision, amid irreconcilable differences over fossil fuels, climate finance and other contentious issues. Disagreements over explicitly mentioning fossil fuels and providing financial support to developing countries ultimately prevented governments from reaching an overarching agreement.European Union, along with several countries, refused to accept the final proposal put forward by the joint Turkish-Australian leadership because it did not explicitly mention fossil fuels. Fossil fuels remained one of the biggest sticking points throughout the negotiations, with Saudi Arabia and other major oil-producing countries lobbying against their inclusion in the final document.

. Director Brad Bird, known for films like Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol has brought to IFFI his sci fi film Ray Gunn. Akashvani correspondent reports that the animated science-fiction film Ray Gunn, combines a detective mystery with themes of prejudice, acceptance and coexistence in a world inhabited by humans and aliens. The film follows private detective Raymond Gunn as he becomes involved in a case surrounding celebrity Venus Nova. The film portrays discriminatory attitudes towards aliens despite their living alongside humans. It explores how differences can become grounds for exclusion and raises questions about belonging.

. Global crude oil prices declined today. Brent crude was trading 0.6 per cent down at 91 US dollars and 44 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.2 per cent down at 82 US dollars and 27 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has sanctioned prosecution against a Private company regarding unsafe packaged drinking water. In a social media post, the food regulator said that a regulatory sample of Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water) was collected from the premises of the company for analysis. FSSAI said that the sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.Upon appeal by the Food Business Operator, the sample was referred to the Referral Food Laboratory, which also declared it unsafe due to the detection of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons. The food regulator said that laboratory findings established violations relating to unsafe food under the Act, following which a sanction was granted to launch prosecution against the company.
